correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary requirements are explicit: the common full-measure set of simultaneous Poisson Lebesgue points depends on f; fixed c is arbitrary. At any such point the original variance vanishes in cones. The peaking automorphism has exact variance 1-|b_a|², norm one, and escapes at fixed interior points. The Möbius inverse identity places its high-variance pseudohyperbolic region in a fixed cone, giving a uniform upper bound. Evaluation at a fixed interior point and at its zero supplies exact complementary lower bounds. Each h_a is VMOA and nonzero with fixed unit Garsia norm, so the strong midpoint condition fails in all four quotients. No nonstandard lemma remains unverified beyond classical Poisson Fatou convergence.

value.rationale: The source expressly asks for strongly extreme points of the natural Garsia-ball geometry. The theorem completely determines their absence for both analytic and nonanalytic BMO and VMO, with a stronger, quantitative-for-every-fixed-c exact max-law. Because all norm-one VMO points are known ordinary extreme points, the conclusion exhibits a nontrivial sharp separation between ordinary and strong extremality. The result is structural and applicable to arbitrary BMO data, not a narrow artificial slice.
